summary:
Marchesa gives the team dethrone and brings back any creature that dies with a +1/+1 counter. The list is built around persist: Murderous Redcap, Glen Elendra, River Kelpie, Puppeteer Clique and Spark Double, reset by Gev, Metallic Mimic, Uncivil Unrest or Thran Vigil, plus free sac outlets and Mikaeus. Draw comes from Satoru, Kelpie and Danny Pink. All 13 attestation items are re-verified; 48 Spellbook lines have all pieces in the canonical list, and representative ones are cited.

Rules surprises: Thran Vigil resets work only on your turn; Uncivil Unrest doubles only the first Redcap shot; deaths during the end step return a turn later, which makes Sneak Attack permanent; Agatha's Soul Cauldron can't share Ashnod's Altar.

interactions.title: Dethrone for the team; creatures with +1/+1 counters return at the next end step
interactions.ruling: Your other creatures have dethrone, so each attack on the player with the most life (or tied) adds a +1/+1 counter before blockers. Each instance triggers separately. Attacking a planeswalker or battle doesn't count. When a creature you control dies with a +1/+1 counter on it, Marchesa sets up a delayed return at the beginning of the next end step. That includes Marchesa herself. If the card leaves the graveyard first, it doesn't return, even if it comes back to the graveyard. If the death happens during an end step, the return waits until the next turn's end step.
interactions.short: Team dethrone; dies with +1/+1 counter → returns at next end step (next turn's if it died during an end step).

oracle.quote: Whenever a creature you control with a +1/+1 counter on it dies, return that card to the battlefield under your control at the beginning of the next end step.

rulings.quote: If the creature card leaves the graveyard before the delayed triggered ability resolves, that card won't return to the battlefield, even if it's back in the graveyard when the delayed triggered ability resolves.
If Marchesa has a +1/+1 counter on it when it dies, it will return to the battlefield under your control because of its own ability.
Dethrone doesn't trigger if the creature attacks a planeswalker, even if its controller has the most life. The same is true if the creature attacks a battle, even if its protector has the most life.

source.item: Marchesa death trigger and delayed return

interactions.title: Persist resets: Gev, Metallic Mimic, Uncivil Unrest, Thran Vigil cancel the -1/-1 counter
interactions.ruling:
A persist creature comes back with a -1/-1 counter. Any +1/+1 counter cancels it as a state-based action, so persist works again:
- **Gev:** an extra counter only if an opponent lost life this turn, one per such opponent.
- **Metallic Mimic:** the chosen creature type (Goblin for Murderous Redcap).
- **Uncivil Unrest:** riot. Choose the counter, not haste.
- **Thran Vigil:** its trigger adds the counter after the creature leaves your graveyard, but only during your turn.

Gev, Mimic and riot put the counter on as the creature enters, together with persist's -1/-1. A creature that enters at the same time as Gev or Mimic doesn't get their counter.
interactions.short: +1/+1 and -1/-1 annihilate, so persist re-arms; Thran Vigil only on your turn.

oracle.quote: Other creatures you control enter with an additional +1/+1 counter on them for each opponent who lost life this turn.
Whenever one or more artifact and/or creature cards leave your graveyard during your turn, put a +1/+1 counter on target creature you control.

rulings.quote: In the case where Gev and one or more other creatures enter at the same time, those creatures won't enter with additional +1/+1 counters, even if one or more opponents lost life this turn.
Creatures of the chosen type that enter the battlefield at the same time as Metallic Mimic won't enter with an additional +1/+1 counter.

spellbook.quote: Thran Vigil triggers, putting a +1/+1 counter on that creature.
An opponent has lost life this turn.

interactions.title: Murderous Redcap loops: Gev / Mimic (Goblin) / Uncivil Unrest, no outlet needed
interactions.ruling:
Redcap enters with a +1/+1 counter and aims its ETB damage at itself. It dies with no -1/-1 counter, so persist returns it. The new -1/-1 counter is cancelled by the next +1/+1 counter, so it dies to its own ETB again, and so on. Each loop is a death and ETB, and Blood Artist, Zulaport Cutthroat or Syr Konrad turns those into the kill.

With Uncivil Unrest, the first Redcap's damage is doubled because it has a counter. Later returns have no counters left after the cancellation, so their damage isn't doubled. Gev's version needs an opponent to have lost life earlier in the turn.
interactions.short: Redcap shoots itself; the +1/+1 source cancels persist's counter → infinite deaths/ETBs.

oracle.quote: When this creature enters, it deals damage equal to its power to any target.
Each other creature you control of the chosen type enters with an additional +1/+1 counter on it.

rulings.quote: The damage is dealt by the same source as the original source of damage. The doubled damage isn’t dealt by Uncivil Unrest unless it was somehow the original source of damage.

spellbook.quote: Murderous Redcap enters, triggering itself, dealing damage to itself equal to its power.
Murderous Redcap dies as a state-based action due to having 0 toughness.

interactions.title: Free sac outlets close any persist reset: Ashnod's, Phyrexian Altar, Altar of Dementia, Goblin Bombardment, Viscera Seer, Carrion Feeder, Yahenni
interactions.ruling:
Any persist creature (Redcap, Glen Elendra Archmage, River Kelpie, Puppeteer Clique) plus any persist reset (marchbr-02) plus any free sac outlet is an infinite loop. The outlet decides the result:
- Ashnod's Altar: infinite colorless mana.
- Phyrexian Altar: infinite colored mana.
- Goblin Bombardment: infinite damage.
- Altar of Dementia: mill.
- Viscera Seer: scry.
- Carrion Feeder: counters.
- Yahenni: indestructible.

Thran Vigil works only on your turn, because its trigger needs cards leaving your graveyard during your turn. The other resets also work on opponents' turns.
interactions.short: Persist creature + reset + free outlet = infinite; outlet picks the payoff.

spellbook.quote: Activate Ashnod's Altar by sacrificing the persist creature.
Activate Phyrexian Altar by sacrificing the persist creature.
Activate Goblin Bombardment by sacrificing the persist creature.

source.item: Altar of Dementia as sacrifice outlet and payoff

interactions.title: Mikaeus, the Unhallowed: undying + persist alternate forever
interactions.ruling: Mikaeus gives your other non-Human creatures undying. Sacrifice a non-Human persist creature: it has no -1/-1 counter, so persist returns it with one. Sacrifice it again: it has no +1/+1 counter, so undying returns it with one. Repeat. Mikaeus's +1/+1 bonus isn't a counter, so it doesn't turn undying off. Marchesa, Mikaeus and Yawgmoth are Human, so they don't get undying. Marchesa's own trigger also fires on the undying-counter deaths, but the immediate return beats her end-step one. Mikaeus + Yawgmoth + Gray Merchant is its own line (Spellbook 328-628-4279).
interactions.short: Non-Human persist creature + Mikaeus + free outlet = infinite (persist ↔ undying).

oracle.quote: Other non-Human creatures you control get +1/+1 and have undying.

rulings.quote: The +1/+1 bonus that Mikaeus gives to other non-Human creatures you control isn’t a counter. It won’t prevent undying from triggering.

spellbook.quote: When the persist creature dies, its undying ability triggers, returning it from your graveyard to the battlefield with a +1/+1 counter on it.

interactions.title: Spark Double copying Glen Elendra / Redcap / Kelpie / Clique
interactions.ruling: Spark Double enters as a copy with an extra +1/+1 counter, so it is its own persist reset. When it dies, persist returns the Spark Double card with a -1/-1 counter. It enters as a fresh copy, and its new +1/+1 counter cancels the -1/-1. So Spark Double + any persist creature + a free outlet loops. Copying Glen Elendra lets you sacrifice it to its own ability ({U}) or to Ashnod's Altar. With River Kelpie, each return from the graveyard draws. With Puppeteer Clique, each return reanimates an opponent's creature (Spellbook 3020-3908-5256 with Altar of Dementia).

rulings.quote: If it copies a planeswalker, Spark Double enters with the appropriate number of loyalty counters as printed on the card plus one. If it copies a creature, Spark Double enters with a +1/+1 counter on it, plus any counters that will be put on it from abilities it copied and other abilities of other objects.

spellbook.quote: As Spark Double enters the battlefield, choose to have it enter the battlefield as a copy of Murderous Redcap with a +1/+1 counter on it.
As Spark Double enters the battlefield, choose to have it enter the battlefield as a copy of Glen Elendra Archmage with a +1/+1 counter on it.

source.item: Spark Double + Glen Elendra Archmage + Ashnod's Altar

interactions.title: Flayer of the Hatebound + Sage of Fables + Ashnod's Altar
interactions.ruling: Sacrifice Flayer to Ashnod's Altar for {C}{C}. Undying returns it with a +1/+1 counter. Flayer entered from your graveyard, so it deals damage equal to its power to any target. Then pay {2} to Sage of Fables to remove that counter and draw, which re-arms undying. The loop is mana-neutral and gives infinite damage. You can hold priority over the draws so you don't deck yourself. Flayer is a Devil, so Sage's Wizard counter doesn't apply.

oracle.quote: Whenever this creature or another creature enters from your graveyard, that creature deals damage equal to its power to any target.
{2}, Remove a +1/+1 counter from a creature you control: Draw a card.

spellbook.quote: Pay {2} to activate Sage of Fables, removing the counter from Flayer and drawing a card.

interactions.title: Sneak Attack + Marchesa: the end-step sacrifice returns a turn later, permanently
interactions.ruling: A Sneak Attacked creature has haste, and it gets a dethrone counter if it attacks the player with the most life. At the beginning of the end step it's sacrificed with the counter on it. Marchesa's delayed return is created during that end step, so it waits for the next turn's end step. Then the creature returns under your control with no sacrifice clause. If the creature left and came back before the end step, Sneak Attack doesn't sacrifice it.
interactions.short: Sneaked creature with a counter returns at the following turn's end step and stays.

oracle.quote: {R}: You may put a creature card from your hand onto the battlefield. That creature gains haste. Sacrifice the creature at the beginning of the next end step.

rulings.quote: You sacrifice the creature only if you still control it. If that creature has left the battlefield, even if it came back, you don't sacrifice it.

source.item: Sneak Attack and Marchesa end-step timing

interactions.title: Return payoffs: Satoru, Twilight Diviner, River Kelpie, Danny Pink
interactions.ruling:
These pay off returns from the graveyard:
- **Satoru:** draws when nontoken creatures enter without being cast, which covers Marchesa, persist and undying returns.
- **Twilight Diviner:** once each turn, makes a token copy of a creature that entered from a graveyard. The token copies the printed card only, with no counters.
- **River Kelpie:** draws whenever any permanent enters from a graveyard.
- **Danny Pink:** gives each creature "draw the first time counters are put on it each turn". Counters a creature enters with count, so riot, Gev and Mimic draws work, and a creature that returns is a new object with a fresh first time.

oracle.quote: Whenever Satoru and/or one or more other nontoken creatures you control enter, if none of them were cast or no mana was spent to cast them, draw a card.
Creatures you control have "Whenever one or more counters are put on this creature for the first time each turn, draw a card."

rulings.quote: The token created by Twilight Diviner's last ability copies exactly what was printed on the original permanent and nothing else (unless that permanent is copying something else; see below). It doesn't copy whether that permanent is tapped or untapped, whether it has any counters on it or Auras and Equipment attached to it, or any non-copy effects that have changed its power, toughness, types, color, and so on.

source.item: Satoru, the Infiltrator with Marchesa returns

interactions.title: Counter tools: Forge of Heroes, Agatha's Soul Cauldron, Unspeakable Symbol, Iron Apprentice, The Ozolith
interactions.ruling:
These keep +1/+1 counters coming:
- **Forge of Heroes:** targets any commander that entered this turn, cast or not, so Marchesa gets her protective counter right away.
- **Agatha's Soul Cauldron:** {T} exiles a card from any graveyard. If it's a creature card, put a +1/+1 counter on a creature, and every creature you control with a counter gains that card's activated abilities. Exiling Ashnod's Altar doesn't work, because it's not a creature card. Exiling Carrion Feeder or Viscera Seer gives your countered creatures a sac outlet.
- **Unspeakable Symbol:** 3 life per counter, at instant speed.
- **Iron Apprentice and The Ozolith:** carry counters over when creatures die.
- **Scorn-Blade Berserker:** backup puts a counter on a target.

oracle.quote: {T}: Choose target commander that entered this turn. Put a +1/+1 counter on it if it's a creature and a loyalty counter on it if it's a planeswalker.
Creatures you control with +1/+1 counters on them have all activated abilities of all creature cards exiled with Agatha's Soul Cauldron.

rulings.quote: Agatha's Soul Cauldron grants only activated abilities. It doesn't grant keyword abilities (unless those keyword abilities are activated), triggered abilities, or static abilities.

source.item: Agatha's Soul Cauldron counter and ability sharing

interactions.title: Flare of Denial pitches a countered blue creature that comes back
interactions.ruling: Flare's alternative cost sacrifices a nontoken blue creature. If it has a +1/+1 counter, Marchesa returns it at the next end step. A persist creature without a -1/-1 counter comes back right away instead. That makes Glen Elendra, Kelpie and Clique nearly free pitches.

oracle.quote: You may sacrifice a nontoken blue creature rather than pay this spell's mana cost.
